jute-fiber.context: A hank of long wavy fibres hanging from a bar with loose ends. Used for natural fibre, burlap and twine materials, sustainable textiles and rope or sack making.

spinneret.context: A flat nozzle plate with fine parallel filaments streaming out below it. Used for synthetic fibre production, textile mills and melt spinning or extrusion processes.

suede-leather.context: A leather square with short brushed nap strokes all in one direction. Used for suede and nubuck material swatches, shoe and jacket fabrics and leather product listings.

patent-leather.context: A leather square crossed by bold diagonal mirror shine streaks. Used for glossy patent leather swatches, dress shoes, handbags and shiny finish descriptions.

vegan-leather.context: A leather hide outline with a small plant leaf inside it. Marks plant-based and cruelty-free leather alternatives on product tags, fashion labels and material guides.

crocodile-leather.context: A leather square embossed with a grid of rectangular scale plates. Used for crocodile and alligator embossed leather swatches, exotic leather goods and bag or belt materials.

snakeskin-leather.context: A leather strip patterned with rows of small diamond scales. Used for snakeskin and python print leather swatches, exotic leather goods and shoe or bag material descriptions.

tannery-vat.context: A round tanning vat filled with liquid and a hide draped over its rim. Used for tanneries, leather making processes, hide curing and traditional craft or industry pages.

hide-stretching-frame.context: A square frame with an animal hide laced to it by cords at the edges. Used for hide drying and stretching, rawhide, parchment making, tanning and traditional leatherwork.

leather-patch.context: A rectangular leather label with a stitched inner border. Used for jean and hat patches, debossed brand labels, personalised tags and garment trims.

shearling.context: A leather panel with a thick curly fleece lining showing along its edge. Used for shearling and sheepskin jackets, boots and slippers, lined coats and warm winter materials.

vellum.context: A translucent sheet with a faint drawing showing through it, with a folded corner. Used for tracing and drafting paper, calfskin parchment, translucent paper and architectural drawings.

crepe-paper.context: A streamer roll with a crinkled strip unrolled below it showing fine ridges. Used for party streamers, paper flowers, craft decorations and gift wrap.

seed-paper.context: A paper square with scattered seeds and a small sprout growing from its top edge. Used for plantable paper, eco greeting cards, wedding favours and biodegradable stationery.

watercolor-paper.context: A spiral-bound sheet with a paint wash stroke and dotted texture. Used for watercolour pads, art supplies, cold press and rough paper, and painting classes.

foam-board.context: A board seen edge-on with a thick foam core between two thin paper faces. Used for foam core display boards, model making, presentation mounting and lightweight signage.

recycled-paper.context: A paper sheet with a folded corner and a circle of chasing arrows in its centre. Used for recycled paper stock, eco stationery, printing options and sustainability labels.

paper-reel.context: A large paper roll on its side with a sheet unwinding flat beneath it. Used for paper mills, newsprint and web printing rolls, packaging paper and industrial paper supply.

tissue-paper.context: Thin soft paper sheets fanned out with a soft fold across the front sheet. Used for gift wrapping, packaging fill, craft tissue and soft thin paper products.

flagstone-paving.context: A ground surface of large irregular stones separated by narrow gaps. Used for patios, garden paths, crazy paving and natural stone landscaping.

ashlar-wall.context: A wall of neat squared cut stone blocks laid in even courses with thin joints. Used for masonry, stone walls, building facades and cut stone construction.

gabion-wall.context: A wire mesh cage box filled with round stones. Used for gabion retaining walls, landscaping, erosion and flood control, and rock filled fencing.

slump-test.context: A truncated metal cone lifted beside a slumped concrete mound, with a marker showing the drop. Used for fresh concrete workability checks, site quality control and construction testing.

concrete-formwork.context: Two wooden form boards with diagonal braces holding a poured concrete wall between them. Used for concrete pours, shuttering, wall forms and building site carpentry.

precast-concrete-panel.context: A flat wall panel with lifting cables rising to a crane hook. Used for precast and prefab construction, tilt-up panels, crane lifts and factory-made concrete elements.

reinforced-concrete.context: A concrete block cross-section with a row of round rebar dots near the bottom. Used for structural engineering, reinforced beams and slabs, rebar and steel reinforcement.

concrete-aggregate.context: A concrete block cross-section showing stones of mixed sizes embedded in it. Used for concrete mix design, gravel and crushed stone, exposed aggregate finishes and cement supplies.

hempcrete-block.context: A rectangular building block with a speckled fibrous face and a hemp leaf on it. Used for hemp lime walls, natural insulation and low-carbon eco construction.

rammed-earth-wall.context: A wall section with wavy compressed soil layers of varying thickness. Used for rammed earth, pise and adobe walls, sustainable building and earth construction.

clay-roof-tile.context: Rows of overlapping rounded roof tiles with staggered joints. Used for terracotta roofing, roof repair and roofing materials, shingles and building supplies.

firebrick.context: A single brick with small flames licking along its top edge. Used for kilns, furnaces and fireplaces, refractory materials and heat-resistant masonry.

hardness-test.context: A pyramid-shaped indenter pressing into a sample and leaving a square dent. Used for indentation hardness testing, Vickers and Brinell methods and materials labs.

scratch-hardness-test.context: A pointed stylus above a stone sample with a scratch line drawn on it. Used for scratch and Mohs hardness testing, mineral identification and coating durability tests.

pendulum-impact-test.context: A swinging pendulum hammer on an arc about to strike a notched bar on supports. Used for Charpy and Izod impact toughness tests and materials laboratories.

compression-test.context: A sample squeezed between two flat plates by arrows pushing inward. Used for compressive strength tests of concrete, foam and packaging in materials labs.

bend-test.context: A bar resting on two supports and bending downward under a centre arrow. Used for flexural and three-point bend tests, beam deflection and weld bend checks.

fatigue-test.context: A bar with a small crack beside a repeating wave that stands for cyclic load. Used for fatigue and endurance testing, repeated stress, crack growth and durability studies.

torsion-test.context: A rod with curved arrows at each end twisting in opposite directions. Used for torsion and torque testing, shear stress studies and shaft or wire twist tests.

shear-test.context: A block split along a line, with opposite arrows sliding the two halves apart. Used for shear strength tests of soil, adhesives and fasteners in materials labs.

drop-test.context: A box falling toward a hard floor with motion lines above it and a height arrow beside it. Used for packaging and product drop tests, impact resistance and shock testing.

abrasion-test.context: A round fabric sample with a looping arrow around a central rubbing head. Used for Martindale abrasion and wear resistance tests on fabrics, leather and coatings.

pilling-test.context: A fabric swatch dotted with small fuzzy balls, next to a magnifier. Used for textile pilling and bobbling checks on knitwear, fleece and upholstery.

colorfastness-test.context: A fabric swatch above a row of grey scale steps running from dark to light. Used for colour fastness, fading and dye bleeding tests on textiles.

shrinkage-test.context: A fabric square with four arrows pointing inward from its sides. Used for wash shrinkage and dimensional stability tests on textiles and garments.

dye-penetrant-test.context: A metal part with a crack line and a spray can misting droplets toward it. Used for dye penetrant inspection, non-destructive crack detection and weld or casting checks.

ultrasonic-flaw-detection.context: A probe on a metal block with sound wave arcs inside and a hidden flaw dot. Used for ultrasonic non-destructive testing, weld and pipe inspection and internal defect detection.

salt-spray-test.context: A test cabinet with a nozzle at the top misting droplets over hanging samples. Used for salt fog and corrosion resistance tests of coatings, metals and fasteners.

uv-weathering-test.context: A sample panel beneath a sun and falling rain. Used for UV ageing, accelerated weathering and outdoor durability tests of plastics, paint and fabrics.

metal-grain-structure.context: A circular microscope view showing irregular polygon grains with boundaries between them. Used for metallography, microstructure analysis and metals and alloys research.

thermal-conductivity.context: A flame at one end of a metal bar with heat wave lines fading along its length. Used for heat conduction, thermal property testing and heat transfer lessons.

burst-test.context: Two clamp blocks gripping a sheet that bulges upward into a dome with an arrow beneath. Used for bursting strength and pressure tests of fabric, paper and membranes.

peel-test.context: A tape strip lifted up from a surface at a right angle with an upward arrow. Used for peel strength and adhesion tests of tapes, labels, films and coatings.

cross-cut-adhesion-test.context: A coated square cut with a lattice of crossing lines and a few flaked squares. Used for cross-hatch paint and coating adhesion tests.

tear-test.context: A fabric square with a ragged tear and arrows pulling the two sides apart. Used for tear strength tests of fabric, film, paper and rubber.

density-test.context: A solid object submerged in a graduated cylinder with the water line marked. Used for density and volume by water displacement, specific gravity and science labs.

waterproof-fabric.context: A fabric swatch with water drops falling onto it. Used for waterproof and water-repellent fabric labels, rainwear and outdoor gear descriptions.

breathable-fabric.context: A fabric layer with wavy vapour lines rising through it. Used for breathable and moisture-permeable textile labels, activewear, outdoor jackets and membranes.

stretch-fabric.context: A fabric swatch pinched in the middle and pulled outward by arrows at both sides. Used for stretch, elastic and spandex fabric labels, leggings and fitted clothing.

flame-retardant-fabric.context: A shield with a flame inside it. Used for flame-retardant and fire-resistant fabric labels, protective workwear, curtains and upholstery safety marks.

antimicrobial-fabric.context: A shield protecting a small bacterium. Used for antimicrobial and antibacterial fabric labels, odour control, hygienic textiles and healthcare linen.

uv-protective-fabric.context: Sun rays bouncing off the surface of a fabric strip. Used for UV protective and UPF-rated clothing labels, sun shirts, swimwear and shade fabrics.

windproof-fabric.context: A fabric layer with wind lines hitting it and curving away. Used for windproof and wind-resistant jacket and shell fabric labels and outdoor gear.

quick-dry-fabric.context: A fabric swatch with a water drop and speed lines leaving it. Used for quick-dry and fast-drying sportswear, travel clothing and towel labels.

moisture-wicking-fabric.context: A fabric layer with drops below it and arrows carrying moisture upward through it. Used for moisture-wicking and sweat-wicking performance fabric labels and activewear.

thermal-insulation-layer.context: Stacked layers on the right with a heat arrow turning back at the outer layer. Used for thermal insulation, warm clothing layers, building insulation and heat retention.

non-slip-surface.context: A sole surface with a row of raised grip teeth. Used for anti-slip and slip-resistant flooring, shoe soles, mats and tread materials.

anti-static-material.context: A fabric square with a crossed-out lightning spark. Used for antistatic and ESD-safe fabrics, clean-room clothing, static-free carpets and electronics handling.

shock-absorbing-material.context: A foam pad pressed by a downward arrow with a spring zigzag inside. Used for cushioning, impact protection, padding, sports gear and packaging materials.

tear-resistant-fabric.context: A reinforced fabric swatch with a grid weave, a small cut that stays closed and arrows pulling on both sides. Used for ripstop and tear-resistant fabric labels and durable outdoor textiles.

recycled-polyester.context: A plastic bottle with an arrow leading to a T-shirt. Used for recycled polyester and rPET fabric labels, bottle-to-clothing sustainability claims and eco apparel.

recycled-rubber-crumb.context: A tyre with an arrow leading to a small pile of rubber granules. Used for recycled tyre rubber, playground and sports surfaces, rubber mulch and tyre recycling.

rag-rug.context: An oval rug made of braided fabric strips coiled in rings. Used for handmade and braided rugs, upcycled textile crafts, floor mats and cosy home decor.

organic-cotton.context: An open cotton boll with a small leaf beside it. Used for organic and sustainable cotton labels, natural fibre clothing, bedding and eco textile certifications.

composite-laminate.context: A slab edge in perspective showing stacked layers. Used for composite and laminate materials such as carbon fibre and fibreglass layups, plies and layered boards.

cane-webbing.context: A square panel of woven cane strands in an open lattice with diagonal strands. Used for rattan and cane chair seats, wicker furniture and woven cane panels.
